sections.html: Pseudanos winterbottomi reaches a length of about 15 cm, so it belongs to the group of medium-sized headstanders. Suggested common name: Striped Bambi Headstander.
The species was imported from Venezuela. Pseudanos winterbottomi and Anostomus ternetzi obviously live together in their natural habitat.
The chemical composition of the water is of no importance. Keep these fish at temperatures between 26 and 28°C.
Like all other headstanders, they do well in large, well-planted aquariums with many hiding places.
The species readily accepts any usual food for ornamental fish. Headstanders need some vegetable matter in their food, otherwise they will destroy aquatic plants.

Young specimens (4-6 cm) kept together in a group were quite peaceful towards each other, and no fin damage occurred. However, at least 10 specimens must be kept together, otherwise they start fighting immediately. Large specimens were kept singly. The youngsters also like to swim in mixed schools with Anostomus ternetzi.

The best company are other headstanders, such as Anostomus ternetzi, but P. winterbottomi can also be kept with other peaceful tetras, cichlids and catfish.

Anostomus ternetzi (golden striped headstander) is widely distributed in South America, recorded from Brazil, French Guyana, Guyana, Suriname and Venezuela. It is among the most peaceful headstanders and stays smaller than Anostomus anostomus, which can exceed 16 cm, while A. ternetzi reaches only about 12 cm. In very young A. ternetzi the broad body band has wavy edges, which later become straight in many specimens; possibly this is a secondary sexual character.

Lexicon: Pseudanos means "false Anostomus". winterbottomi honours Richard Winterbottom, curator emeritus for ichthyology at the Royal Ontario Museum, Canada.
